title: Smoot-Hawley, 1930: the tariff that made the Great Depression worse
short: Smoot-Hawley: the 1930 tariff that made the Depression worse
dek: A limited fix for farmers became duties on nearly 3,300 goods, retaliation from trading partners and a 66% collapse in world trade. Why the 1930 law is still the benchmark for every trade war.
card: US tariffs on dutiable goods hit 59.1% by 1932, and world trade fell 66%. The story of history's most famous tariff.
hero_src: Data: Douglas Irwin (NBER), US Office of the Historian
sources: Douglas A. Irwin, 'The Hawley-Smoot Tariff and the Great Depression, 1928–1932', in Clashing over Commerce (NBER / University of Chicago Press)
